newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Norilsk says Moscow delays ore supply to Italy.
newsitem.headline: Norilsk says Moscow delays ore supply to Italy.

text.p: Russia's Norilsk Nickel said on Friday it was having problems getting government permission to export nickel and copper concentrates for refining at an Italian metals plant.
Norilsk spokesman Anatoly Komrakov said the concentrates contained precious metals whose export by companies was forbidden under Russian law.

Norilsk had an agreement with Osmium Holdings to supply the concentrates. Osmium is a British-U.S. investors' group hoping to buy Italy's Crotone zinc smelter and convert it into a nickel and copper refinery running at least partly on Norilsk concentrates.
But Komrakov said the Russian government had so far not given permission for a trial shipment of several hundred tonnes of concentrates.
"As far as I know, we cannot get government permission to export a trial shipment because it contains some amounts of precious metals and the law says those metals cannot be exported," he said.
"There is some hope we may be able to convince the government to let us send the stuff out."

Osmium signed a deal with Norilsk last year to process 11 million tonnes of low-grade concentrates in Russia, using tailings dams full of residue, and then to ship the material to the Italian plant for refining.
Komrakov said Norilsk was interested in the deal because it involved leaching processes using heat-loving bacteria that could not function at Norilsk's frozen headquarters north of the Arctic.
"Because of our geography, we have to take the ore to the microbes, not the microbes to the ore," he said. "The assaying must be carried out in a warm climate."

Osmium's representative, Bankside Consultants, had said earlier this week Norilsk was rethinking its deal with Osmium because the Russian metals giant may want to process the tailings and concentrates on its own.
Komrakov said Norilsk had built up stocks of tailings over the past 10 years but had not used them because it had richer ores to work and lacked some needed processing technology.
Norilsk is one of the world's leading producers of nickel and platinum group metals, as well as of copper and cobalt.
